explanation: The L90M substitution reduces saquinavir affinity through a long-range allosteric effect rather than direct contact; the methionine's slightly reduced hydrophobicity and smaller side-chain volume (3.8 Å³ loss) at the C-terminal dimer interface destabilizes the precise geometric organization of the protease dimer, which propagates conformational changes that subtly perturb the active site geometry or ligand-binding pocket accessibility at a distance of ~8 Å. Although L90M makes no direct contacts with the inhibitor, the loss of optimal hydrophobic packing in this dimer-stabilizing region decreases the energetic favorability of the competent binding-ready conformation, raising the entropic cost of accommodating saquinavir's bulky scaffold.
